request.spec:
A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today (a hold whose dates include today) gets no cut
from any pool, and their share is spread over the other members with a cut in proportion to those
members' shares: each member's cut is the pot times their share divided by the shares of the members
with a cut, added up, rounded half to even, with the remainder to the largest share as before (when
no member is left with a cut, each shows 0.00). The pool's total share and balance are unchanged by
the hold.

agent.result_text:
A person on hold on the sheet's today now gets no cut from any pool, and their share is spread over the members who still get one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The change is all on the server, in two files:

- **`pool/PoolService.java`**
  - Each pool member now records whether the person has a hold covering the sheet's today. A member that is a pool is never treated as held.
  - Each cut is the pot × the member's share ÷ the shares of the members with a cut, added up, rounded half to even.
  - Members with a cut are those who are neither held nor retired.
  - The leftover cent goes to the largest share among those members, as before; if no one has a cut, every cut shows 0.00.
  - The pool's total share and balanced flag still count held members, so the hold doesn't change them.
- **`person/Person.java`**: added `heldOn(LocalDate)`, which says whether any of the person's holds covers that date.

No change was needed to the stored data or the front end: the front end already adds up each person's pool cuts for `person-cut-total`, so the new figures show there automatically. No new audit records were needed either.

Before this change the cuts divided by 100. That gives the same numbers as the new rule whenever nobody is held, because a balanced pool's counted shares already total 100.
